note: Adapted from Desneux's report on the Saharan termites collected by Lameere; the original is in French (a Latin diagnosis + French description). The main text describes only the large soldier (grand soldat) and the alate (imago alata); it notes that the workers (ouvriers) are hard to distinguish from the larvae and are not described separately, and the small soldier is not described. The page numbers follow the numbers at the head of the pages (437—438). Fig. 1 (head and pronotum of the large soldier) is not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Large soldier slender, pale yellow, shining, head reddish brown; head large, oblong, flattened, from the clypeus to the anterior margin of the pronotum slightly longer than wide, concave in the middle, with a round fontanelle pore in the centre of the concavity, the rim of the pore blackish brown and distinct; on each side at the midpoint of the imaginary line from the fontanelle to the inner edge of antennal segment 1 there is a small, often slightly darker swelling; eyes degenerate, reduced to a dark dot behind the antennal socket; labrum extremely developed and swollen, about three-fifths of the head length; mandibles stout, their tips curved inwards and turned up, the right mandible with 3—4 lateral teeth (the first stronger), the left mandible with about 5 teeth of unequal size; antennae (15)—16-segmented, gradually tapering towards the tip. Alate: wing span 19—20 mm, body length (including head) about 6 mm; on the degree of separation of the media and submedia of the fore wing and the wing surface being only slightly smoky it can be distinguished from related species.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large soldier: body slender, pale yellow (jaune flave), shining, head reddish brown. Head large, oblong, flattened, from the clypeus to the anterior margin of the pronotum slightly longer than wide; concave in the middle, with a small round pore (the fontanelle) in the centre of the concavity, the rim of the pore blackish brown and very distinct; on each side at the midpoint of the imaginary line from the fontanelle to the inner edge of antennal segment 1 there is a small, often slightly darker swelling. Eyes degenerate, reduced to a dark dot behind the antennal socket. Labrum very developed and swollen, about three-fifths of the head length, nearly circular, prolonged forwards into a triangle (this prolongation is yellowish in some specimens), slightly darker than the head, bearing long pale hairs. Mandible base brown, the tip and part of the inner margin black, at least as long as the head without the labrum, the basal half wide and swollen; right mandible with 3 or 4 lateral teeth, the first stronger; left mandible with several small teeth of unequal size (5 on average); in front of these teeth the mandible is prolonged into a single slender tooth curved inwards and turned up. Antennae about as long as the head with the mandibles, evenly tapering from base to tip, stiff, bearing long hairs; (15)—16-segmented, segment 1 large and swollen, segment 2 small and almost twice as long as wide, segment 3 more than two to three times as long as segment 2, hardly swollen in front and nearly cylindrical, the following segments also slender, the last few nearly conical and progressively shorter. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head, trapezoidal, narrowed posteriorly, the corners rounded, the anterior margin notched in the middle; the sides flattened, the margin slightly upcurved. Mesonotum slightly narrower than the pronotum, more oval, shorter. Metanotum shorter still, not clearly separated from the abdominal segments. Legs very short and stout; femora short and wide, obtusely kidney-shaped, laterally compressed; tibiae gradually stouter from the base to the middle and tapering towards the tip, the tip with 3 dark brown spines on the first pair of legs and 2 on each of the other two pairs. Terminal abdominal appendages very short, conical. Body sparsely covered with pale hairs. In some specimens the head has no distinct median concavity; in others the mandibles are shorter.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Latin description: body dark brown, head and pronotum darker; head oval, narrowed in front, with a point projecting in the middle; frons with two pale spots in front of the ocelli; clypeus paler than the frons, swollen; compound eyes medium-sized, ocelli elongate, almost their own long diameter away from the compound eyes; antennae 14-segmented, segments 1, 2 and 3 almost equal in length; pronotum almost as wide as the head (with the compound eyes), nearly semicircular, with a notch in the middle of the posterior margin, the anterior margin straight; the posterior margins of the meso- and metanota deeply incised in the middle, the lobes rounded and darker; wings slightly smoky, the veins hardly visible, the costal margin brown; abdomen pale, darker at the sides. Measurements: wing span 19—20 mm; body length (including head) about 6 mm. French description: upper surface dark brown, head and pronotum darker; head oval, narrowed and slightly flattened in front, with a distinctly projecting point (the fontanelle point) between the eyes; frons with two pale spots in front of the ocelli; clypeus paler than the frons, swollen, its anterior margin almost straight and the sides rounded; the first two mandibular teeth about equal in length; compound eyes medium-sized.
